translations.text: By our holy father John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople.
On the holy apostle Thomas, and against the Arians. To the law of the Church,
in submission, I pledged myself. As far as it is possible to proceed [?], we are formed by the greatness of the instruction.
I shrink back in fear and am restrained on every side. How shall I approach this deed?
Or what outlet shall I find for my speech? If I proclaim Thomas alive, the tomb, on the contrary, proclaims
death. If I confess him dead, his deeds contradict me. He is dead
and yet without death. He died as a man and passes through the world like an angel. He suffered
and withstands sufferings. He lies below and appears above, for nothing could conceal him.
No place could destroy him. His tombs embraced the whole inhabited world,
and everywhere he shines like the sun. The relics of the righteous man divided up the earth.
He appeared more expansive than all creation, and grace exalted him in the world.
Every land has a part of Thomas. He has filled the whole world and remains whole in these places. Into all
the earth his glory has gone out, and his presence to the ends of the inhabited world. What, then, shall I call him?
The sun? Yet night does not overshadow him. A star? Yet day does not hide it.
At all times he illuminates the created world. He has driven all darkness from the inhabited world.
There is no darkness after him; darkness will not darken him. A river does not stop him; the sea cannot hold him. The surrounding sea knows the man.
People of other tongues honor Thomas. All lands celebrate today
and offer this saying as a gift to the Master: “My Lord and my God, my kinsman and my Creator,
my Redeemer and my King.” For Thomas taught these things.
He left this to us as to his own children [?]. Nature holds the saying like a treasure.
The whole human race is strengthened by that utterance. The saying has reached as far as the angels.
The archangels hold this confession like an anchor.
All creation carries this proclamation about as a binding obligation. Arius alone deprives himself of the saying.
He alone falls away from his allotted share. He does not confess the Lord Christ together with Thomas.
He does not acknowledge him as God together with Thomas. He calls the Master a slave; he calls him neither Lord nor God.
He does not uphold the truth. He does not agree with Thomas. He does not follow the righteous man.
Yet he honors his days and celebrates together with the whole inhabited world, joining Thomas’s companions.
But wickedness will not steal away good deeds. The deceiver will not seize the guide to truth. The shepherd knows the wild beasts.
The slinger knows the wolf. The helmsman knows the wave. The harbor knows the storm. The soldier knows the enemy. He knows—
Thomas knows Arius. He knows him and drives him away. He does not accept honor from a deceiver.
He does not enter a murderer’s cave. He will not dwell with him.
He turns away from the assembly of those who deny the faith. He loathes their contentious voice.
He hates mouths that speak falsehood against God. He checks
the tongue that does not call Christ Lord and God, and cries out to them from throughout the inhabited world:
“Arius, why do you [?] me? Why do you anoint my head with oil? Why do you celebrate my day, you lawless man?
I do not accept your lawless praise. I do not agree with your empty faith.
I do not acknowledge your lawless teachings. Do not honor me while dishonoring the Creator. I do not accept honor that is the mother of dishonor.
If you revile the Master, how can you persuade me, his servant? If you do not hold my faith, how can you celebrate my memory?
If you do not agree with me, how can you have fellowship with my tomb?
I came to know him as Lord and Christ and God. I examined his hand and found the truth.
With my own fingers I became certain. No one else told me what I know. I do not know the miracle merely by hearsay.
I did not believe those who spoke; I opposed the apostles. I provoked Peter when he wanted to teach me.
I said, ‘Man, why do you trouble me? Why do you give me words in place of deeds? Why do you tell me to believe on the strength of a report?
Just as you saw, I too will see. Just as you learned, I too will learn, if I am to preach.
Only after seeing will I preach. No one proclaims hearsay. No one brings testimony based on a report.
No one will accept me if I recount what you have told me. If they ask me how Christ rose, I do not know
what I will say. If I say, “Peter told me,” who should be believed first? I will see and proclaim.
I will learn and teach. I will believe and lead others to believe. I will say, “I am Thomas, an apostle,
not from men, nor from a man, nor for a man’s sake.”’ While I was saying this, Christ appeared and immediately resolved the dispute.
He said to me, ‘What has happened, Thomas? Why do you oppose Peter? Why do you argue with the others?’
Come, test the miracle. Learn the resurrection through action. Bring your hand near and see the flesh.
If you can, take hold of it, if your fingers are clean. Touch the form; if you believe, you will reach it.
But if you [?], you will not find it. If you harbor passion, you will not know the one who is free from passion. Hearing this,
I cleansed my soul of unbelief. I stripped myself of contentious knowledge.
Submitting, I now took hold. I touched the flesh, rejoicing and trembling.
Along with my fingers, I opened the eye of my soul, and through both actions I came to understand.
I held and saw. I examined and looked. With my hands I held the flesh,
but with my soul I recognized God. Outwardly I found something miraculous,
and inwardly something awesome. What appeared was great, and what was held was wondrous.
Then, astonished at the one I had received, I cried out, “My Lord and my God!” For I saw no slave; there was nothing lowly in his appearance.
His form and kinship shone, and his divinity blazed forth. What was borne was exalted,
and the one bearing it was glorified. In both activities that were perceived, it was the person who was worshiped.
These things I received after testing them; these things I held with my finger. But where, Arius, did you learn your deception?
Where did you learn what you proclaim? Have you examined Christ as I have?
Have you laid your hand upon him? Have you investigated his forms? Do your fingers bear witness for you? Did you receive the Lord?
With which hand? With the one with which you seized property entrusted to you? With which you robbed the apostles?
With which you took a Gentile’s plunder? With which you held dishonorable payment?
With which you [?] judgments of blood? With which you thought it right to do wrong?
Did you examine Christ with that hand? May it never be! The Master is not so unjust. Christ is not so deceived
that he would entrust his flesh to you. You have not held the one you rejected.
You have not examined the one you hated. You have not investigated the one you disparaged. You have not seen the one you did not believe.
If you had investigated properly, you would not have interpreted so badly. If you had confessed him, you would not have been so unbelieving.
Go away and delight in wickedness. Fall away with your fellow adversaries. Yet I have overthrown your one son [?].
Yet I have freed the people from your malice. A little longer, and I will overthrow you everywhere.
A little longer, and I will drive you from the inhabited world. Now I will take off your head.
Now [?] I will deliver the West too from your malice. Yes, blessed Thomas, fulfill your word in deed.
Follow your own voice. Bring your good beginning to completion. Just as you freed the East,
free the West too. Hear also the robber, as also the evildoer, as also the evildoer who has been cut off [?].
Crown the emperors with victory. Give peace to the people.
Accept the sweat of those who have gathered. Accept the city as it prays to your dust. All bodies have sent up a prayer to you.
Old and young, we fall before your tomb. Maidens and young men, we embrace your body.
Infants, like young birds, look toward you with open mouths. Do not disregard this sight.
Do not let our labors go unrewarded. Give us a fitting reward for our sweat.
We ask nothing great of you. We ask you for what you have. We seek what you give.
We await what you wish to see: the foreigner departed, Arius driven away,
the emperor crowned, the world converted, Christ exalted, and from the whole inhabited world together,
hearing and saying, “My Lord and my God!” To him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
